text:
maya: quick ask — can someone from runtime/infra/security take a fast look at PR #7721? small change to the batcher eviction + kernel selector logic, want to merge today if green. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7721 :pray:

sam: @maya linked — I'm around, can you drop a 1-2 line summary of the risk and why it needs to land today? :eyes:

maya: tl;dr: fixes a corner-case where KV cache eviction triggered while a contiguous KV prefetch was inflight, could lead to double-free in our kernel path. added a guard and a test that reproduces the race. no interface changes. goal is to avoid a flakey prod regression that popped in canary yesterday.

li: pinging infra — does this touch any deploy infra/configs or driver updates? or is it purely runtime code?

maya: purely runtime code in serving/runtime/kv_cache.{cpp,hh} + kernel selector. no driver or infra config touches.

ashley: security quick question — does this change any serialization or deserialization boundaries, or touch external input parsing? also need to know if it adds any new permissions (KMS, network) or new env vars.

maya: nope on deserialization. it's internal cache lifecycle only. no new perms, no new env. I added an assertion and tightened lifetime handling.

sam: ok i'll do a runtime pass now. main thing I'll check is the new guard isn't going to increase latency on hot path — if you have a microbenchmark that reproduces perf numbers pls attach.

maya: attaching results from local perf run: `bench/kernel_kv_eviction --iters 1000` shows <1% median delta in token latency, p95 +0.6ms under extreme synthetic load. posted raw CSV in the PR.

ci-bot: CI passed — all checks green (unit, integration, perf smoke).

li: I'll sanity-check the rollout plan — if sam signs off we should gate the merge on a small canary to dedicated pool for 2 hours. If autopromote is configured we can do automatic fallback to model-variant-old on errors.

maya: agreed. plan in PR description: canary tag -> monitor latency/errors for 2 hours -> if ok, promote. If anything spikes, auto-fallback to previous build is enabled.

sam: reviewed. left one nit (guard variable name) and one optional comment about microbench harness location. nothing blocking. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks @sam. @ashley @li can we get approvals? I'm going to hold merge until both OK.

ashley: security reviewed — no red flags, marking as approved.

li: infra okay with canary rollout and fallback. approving from infra side.

maya: awesome — merging after 10m to give anyone else a last chance. thanks all :rocket:

ci-bot: deploy job started for canary (canary-pool-4). monitoring hooks active.
